name: Fish Tycoon Fix Patcher
description: Repairs Crimson Comet curing, fixes Unknown Chemical uses, and lets the exact supported supplies stack in slots 2-4.

settings.name: Fix Vanilla Bugs
settings.summary: Fixes stock bugs: the Plant of Incubation and Plant of Nutrition do what their names say, and the Golden Seahorse has full health and food.
settings.description: Fixes bugs in the base game. The store's two plants do each other's job: the Plant of Incubation ($200, "increases the viability of purchased eggs") actually rescues starving fish (on Random(100) <= 20 per step, food +5), and the Plant of Nutrition ($350) actually adds 1 egg to every egg batch. Their effects are swapped back: the Plant of Incubation adds the egg and the Plant of Nutrition rescues starving fish. Names, pictures and prices are unchanged, and plants already bought switch to their proper effect. The Golden Seahorse arrives with full health and a full food meter (the base game gives it health 80-94 and food 50), and a seahorse already in a save is filled up the first time the save is loaded with this setting. The game never lowers a seahorse's meters, so it stays full; nothing else about it changes.

settings.name: Crimson Comet 20% curing fix
settings.summary: The Crimson Comet magic fish cures a sick fish 20% of the time, as it was meant to. In the base game it never cures anything.
settings.description: Repairs the cure roll, which the base game can never pass. The original code calls its random helper with an upper bound of 0, so no roll can come back under the threshold and a Crimson Comet never cures anything. The call is redirected to a wrapper that rolls 0-99 once per eligible diseased fish and cures on 0-19, a flat 20 percent. The disease clear and the cure counter behind it are the original code, unchanged. Touches 2 places: VA 0x4204CE and a 14-byte wrapper at VA 0x401E11.

settings.name: Unknown Chemical: 3 uses
settings.summary: One Unknown Chemical purchase lasts three uses instead of one.
settings.description: Makes one Unknown Chemical purchase last three uses instead of one. The base game rewrites the remaining count to 1 every time the item is used, so simply raising the purchase amount would be undone on first use; that 10-byte write at VA 0x4210B7 is replaced with NOPs so the purchased count survives and decrements normally. The store text is corrected to match, in English ('Contains 3 doses.') and German ('Reicht für 3 Behandlungen.'). Touches 3 places.

settings.name: Universal supply slots 2-4
settings.summary: Medicines, chemicals and fish eggs can go in any of supply slots 2-4, instead of each being locked to its own slot (with DS Store Items, Exotic Fish Eggs too).
settings.description: Lets the eight supported medicines, chemicals, and egg types share supply slots 2-4 instead of each being locked to its own slot. Buying an item first looks for a matching stack in slots 2-4, then the first empty slot, and only then asks to replace something. The normal Buy confirmation still appears and cancelling changes nothing. Using an item swaps its record into the slot the original handler expects and swaps it back, so effects still run exactly once. Adds a 961-byte routine at the end of .text (VA 0x43F2A0) and rewrites the slot prompts to say 'item' in English and German. Touches 14 places. With DS Store Items on, Exotic Fish Eggs follow the same rules: they stack, take the first empty slot, and hatch from any of slots 2-4.
settings.warning: Changing this setting on a save that already has supplies: the base game gives every purchase a count of 3 and then throws the item away after one use, while this setting counts uses down. An egg or Unknown Chemical bought before the setting was turned on therefore lasts 3 uses once it is on, and items stacked or moved to another slot while it was on can misbehave after it is turned off (a stack of eggs is used up by one hatch; an item outside its own slot may not work). Use up slots 2-4 before switching this setting on or off. Modded copies keep the same executable name when you re-patch, so they keep using the same saves.

settings.name: Buy Multiple Golden Seahorses
settings.summary: Lets you buy the Golden Seahorse again, and more than one, if you trash or lose it. With DS Store Items on, the store animals can be bought more than once too.
settings.description: Allows purchasing of multiple Golden Seahorses, in case you trash or lose it somehow. The base game blocks a second purchase in three separate places, all keyed off the ownership dword at state + index*20 + 0x78: the store click handler refuses at VA 0x4282CA, the purchase routine returns before charging at VA 0x427B66, and the panel shows 'This is in your inventory.' instead of the price at VA 0x42735C. Each is wrapped so store item 11, the Golden Seahorse, takes the normal buy path while every other item keeps its original behaviour exactly. Touches 7 places.

settings.name: Bigger tanks: 30 fish
settings.summary: Every tank holds 30 fish instead of 21, the selling tank too; each fish sells with the stock odds.
settings.description: Raises every tank (Tank One, Tank Two and the selling tank) from 21 fish to 30. Each tank's block in the game's state already has room for 31 fish records and the save already stores all of them, so nothing about the save changes; the game simply only ever used the first 21. Every place that assumes 21 is raised, so fish 22-30 get everything fish 1-21 get: adding a fish, the swimming fish on screen, the per-step update (age, food, health, sickness, breeding, death), new game, the magic-fish check, thought bubbles, medicines, chemicals and growth hormone, customers, the selling screen, the starter-egg check and the sickness crowding count. Every adult in the selling tank is for sale with the stock odds per fish, and as in the stock game at most one fish sells a second; the crowd counts at most 21 adults (the stock game's most), so no fish's odds go past the stock game's best. The isolation tank still holds one fish. With DS Store Items on, the store's animals live in their own file beside the save, so they never take a fish's place. Touches 28 places in the game's code, plus one short routine for the crowd. See docs/fish-tycoon-tank-expansion.md.
settings.warning: Turning this off while a tank holds more than 21 fish hides the fish in slots 22-30 until it is on again. Sell or move fish down to 21 per tank before switching it off.

settings.name: Maximizable window
settings.summary: In windowed mode the game's window can be maximized or resized; the picture scales to fit, keeping its shape.
settings.description: Turns on the Maximize button on Fish Tycoon's window in windowed mode, and lets you drag its edges to resize it. At any size other than the game's own, the picture is scaled to fill the window with its shape kept (black bars where it does not fit) and smoothed, and the mouse lands where you point. Restore the window and it is the normal size again, drawn exactly as before. Fullscreen is unchanged. Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start; saves are unchanged.

files.destination: Fish Tycoon Fix Patcher DLLs/Maximizable Window.dll

settings.name: DS Exclusive Fish
settings.summary: Adds the Nintendo DS version's 7 extra fish bodies and 7 extra fins: 343 new species, reached through the Unknown Chemical and the Magic Fish of Mutation.
settings.description: Adds the seven bodies and seven fins only the Nintendo DS version has: Clownfish, Discus, Bicolor, Trigger, Surgeonfish, Tang and Idle bodies, and Small Fin, Roundy, Angel, Clown, Yellow, Blue and Moorish fins, 343 new species in all. Eggs, the store and breeding two PC fish never give them. The Unknown Chemical, and the Magic Fish of Mutation at hatching, can now step a Spotanus body or a Twin-Fin fin one place further, into the DS ones, with the same odds as before. Breeding a DS fish follows the DS game: the parents' average, an odd total rounded up or down at random. Prices, rarity (most need environment level 3), names and fin placement follow the DS game. Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start; new sprites go in Images, and each save slot keeps its DS species data in a separate file beside the save. See docs/fish-tycoon-ds-fish-testing-guide.md.
settings.warning: Turning this off after DS fish are in a save leaves those fish with genes the game cannot draw or name. Sell or trash every DS fish before switching it off.

files.destination: Fish Tycoon Fix Patcher DLLs/DS Exclusive Fish.dll

settings.name: DS Store Items
settings.summary: Adds an Upgrades page to the Supplies store with the DS version's store items: the Magic Pufferfish, Blue-Spotted Stingray and Moray Eel (with its rock), tank animals that help your fish without taking a fish's place, and Exotic Fish Eggs that hatch only DS fish. Needs DS Exclusive Fish.
settings.description: Adds an Upgrades button to the Supplies store with the Nintendo DS version's store items. The Magic Pufferfish, Blue-Spotted Stingray and Moray Eel are tank companions like the Golden Seahorse: they swim in your tank, can be dragged between tanks, never age, breed or get sold, and magically enhance the life and environment of your fish (the exact effects are in the Tools tab's Game Mechanics). The Moray Eel comes with its rock, a decoration you can move: drop the eel on its rock to send it home, and drag it out by its head. Trashing the eel trashes its rock, and the other way round. The animals never take a fish's place: each tank has 5 animal places of its own, the Golden Seahorse's included, kept beside the save in "Tank Animals <slot>.dat" (a save from an earlier build has its animals moved there the first time it loads). Exotic Fish Eggs ($2300) hatch only the DS-exclusive bodies and fins. The Golden Seahorse keeps its PC effects and gains its DS one. Needs DS Exclusive Fish.
settings.warning: Turning this off hides the store animals and the Golden Seahorse: they wait in "Tank Animals <slot>.dat" beside the save and come back when it is on again. The eel's rock stays in the tank as a sprite the game cannot draw; trash the eel (its rock goes with it) before switching it off if you mind.

files.destination: Fish Tycoon Fix Patcher DLLs/DS Store Items.dll

settings.name: Time Warp
settings.summary: Adds a Time Warp item to the store's Upgrades screen: $500 to skip 1-72 hours, as if you had been away.
settings.description: Adds a Time Warp item (a clock) to the Supplies store's Upgrades page (DS Store Items), which this setting turns on. Clicking it asks, in a small Windows popup, how many hours should pass (1 to 72), then asks Yes/No and charges a flat $500. Then every fish in all four tanks ages with every check (health, sickness, food, breeding and births), and research progresses, exactly as if you had been away that many real-life hours, with no catch-up cap. Plants or fish can starve, dry out or die along the way, as they would while you were away. Refused while time is stopped. Saves keep their layout.

files.destination: Fish Tycoon Fix Patcher DLLs/Time Warp.ini

settings.name: Free upgrades
settings.summary: Every item on the store's Upgrades screen costs $0.
settings.description: Every item on the Supplies store's Upgrades page (DS Store Items), which this setting turns on, costs $0: the Magic Pufferfish, Blue-Spotted Stingray and Moray Eel ($1250 each), Exotic Fish Eggs ($2300), and the Time Warp clock ($500) and Add Money ($950) when those settings are on. The price shown says $0 and no money is taken. Everything else stays: The Puffer Fish, Sting Ray and Moray Eel are still one of each in your tanks (unless Buy Multiple Golden Seahorses is on), the eggs still need a free slot, and the game's own purchase confirmations are still asked. The game's own store items keep their prices. Saves keep their layout.

settings.name: Add Money cheat ($1,000)
settings.summary: Adds a +$1,000 item to the store's Upgrades screen: pay $950, get $1,000, as often as you like.
settings.description: Adds a pile of gold coins, +$1,000, in the net next to the Time Warp clock on the Supplies store's Upgrades page (DS Store Items), which this setting turns on. It costs $950 ($0 with Free upgrades), is bought like the other items there (the price is shown, you need the money, and you confirm), and then adds $1,000 to your money: $50 more each time, or $1,000 with Free upgrades. It can be bought any number of times. Money never goes past the game's own maximum. Saves keep their layout.

patches.note: Same field and value as the slots variant, applied when Golden Seahorse is on and universal slots is off, so the wrappers at VA 0x43F800-0x43F837 are mapped. Shipped as 0x40000 in v1.0.6-v1.0.8, which overlapped .rdata and made Windows reject the executable outright.

Same field and value again, applied when Golden Seahorse and universal slots are both on, covering the payload at 0x43F2A0 and the wrappers at 0x43F800 together. Shipped as 0x40000 in v1.0.6-v1.0.8 with the same loader-fatal overlap.

VA 0x4204CE. The base game calls its exclusive-upper-bound RNG helper at VA 0x403240 with 0, so the roll can never fall below any threshold and the cure never fires. The 5-byte call is retargeted to the wrapper at VA 0x401E11.

patches.expected: CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC CC
patches.note: VA 0x401E11, written into 0xCC alignment padding. Assembles to: push 100; call the same RNG helper at 0x403240; pop ecx; cmp al,20; setb al; ret. It returns true for rolls 0-19 out of 0-99, a 20 percent cure chance per eligible diseased fish. The original (11,11) scanner, disease clear, and counter increment are left untouched.

VA 0x4210B7. Replaces the 10-byte instruction 'mov dword ptr [eax+0x2F8], 1' with ten NOPs. That instruction rewrote the active chemical count to 1 on every use, which would reset a three-use purchase the first time it was used. Removing it preserves the count the purchase path established. The matching decrement at VA 0x421305 stays in place.

The same ten-NOP replacement at VA 0x4210B7, selected when universal slots is on without the three-use setting, so stacked one-dose purchases decrement normally instead of being reset to 1 on each use.
The same ten-NOP replacement at VA 0x4210B7, selected when both settings are on, so stacked three-dose purchases decrement normally.
English store description string in .rdata at file 0x458C9. 'Contains one dose.' becomes 'Contains 3 doses.', matching what the three-use setting actually grants. Same byte length, null-padded.

German store description string in .rdata at file 0x45854. 'Reicht für eine Behandlung.' becomes 'Reicht für 3 Behandlungen.', the wording the game already uses for Growth Hormone's three doses. One byte shorter, null-padded to the same length.

PE section table, .text VirtualSize (file 0x1F8). Raises it from 0x3E29F to 0x3F000 so the slots payload at VA 0x43F2A0-0x43F660 falls inside mapped memory. 0x3F000 is the largest legal value: .text starts at RVA 0x1000, so 0x1000+0x3F000 = 0x40000, exactly where .rdata begins. Anything larger overlaps .rdata and Windows refuses to load the image. Raw size, file size, and SizeOfImage are unchanged.

961-byte payload at VA 0x43F2A0-0x43F660, written into verified zero padding at the end of .text. It holds the store-purchase routine (search slots 2-4 for a matching stack, then the first empty slot, then the replacement prompt), the item-use trampoline at VA 0x43F550 that swaps a 28-byte slot record into the slot the original handler expects and back again, and the shared egg decrement routine at VA 0x43F630. This variant adds one use per Unknown Chemical purchase.

The same 961-byte payload at VA 0x43F2A0-0x43F660, selected when the Unknown Chemical three-use setting is also on. Identical except that an Unknown Chemical purchase adds three uses to the stack instead of one.

VA 0x428133. Replaces 'cmp edi,0x19 / ja +0x9A', the gate that accepted only store indices 0-7 for slot placement, with a 5-byte jump to the payload at VA 0x43F2A0 plus four NOPs. The payload still shows the original localized Buy confirmation (string ID 0xEC) and cancels with no change unless the player answers Yes.

VA 0x420B70. Replaces the item-use handler's 8-byte prologue with a jump to the trampoline at VA 0x43F550 plus NOPs. The trampoline swaps the chosen slot record into the slot the original handler expects, calls that unmodified handler, then swaps the records back, so item effects run exactly once and are not duplicated.

VA 0x4213A7. The original 42-byte block cleared the entire egg record on hatch. It becomes 'call 0x43F630' (the shared decrement, which removes one use and clears the record only at zero) followed by a jump to the original hatch continuation at VA 0x4213D1, then NOPs. Using call rather than jmp is deliberate: the shared routine ends in ret and needs a matching pushed return address. v1.2.0-v1.2.3 used jmp here and crashed with EIP 0x00000003.
VA 0x421476. The same replacement for the unusual egg path, continuing at VA 0x4214A0.
